analysis.description: The paper proposes to unify likelihood-free inference and black-box optimization under a probabilistic framework that aids in the design of biological sequences. The authors introduce various new algorithms and demonstrate their empirical effectiveness on sequence design tasks.

type.justification: The paper involves systematic experiments on various sequence design benchmarks to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology, which is typical of empirical studies.
type.quote: To demonstrate the empirical effectiveness of our methods, we conduct systematical experiments to evaluate their performance on four in-silico sequence design benchmarks.

name.justification: The research primarily focuses on designing biological sequences, viewed as a black-box optimization problem, under a probabilistic framework.
name.quote: In this work, we focus on an important subdomain: de novo biological sequence design.

name.justification: One of the main contributions of the paper is the unification of likelihood-free inference with black-box optimization.
name.quote: We develop a probabilistic framework by reformulating the aforementioned black-box optimization target as a posterior modeling problem.

name.justification: The paper considers biological sequence design as a black-box optimization problem and unifies it with likelihood-free inference.
name.quote: In this work, we deem sequence design to be a black-box optimization problem.

name.quote: Interestingly, this is the proposed sequence design algorithm in Gupta & Zou (2019), where the authors name this kind of updating “feedback” because training of the parametric generator q φ (m) exploits feedback signals from the oracle. In this paper, we follow Brookes & Listgarten (2018) to crystallize q φ (m) to be a variational autoencoder (Kingma & Welling, 2014), and use the term Feedback-Variational AutoEncoder (FB-VAE) to refer to Algorithm 2.
